title: Grade 5
blurb: Unit-by-unit practice for the whole Grade 5 year — place value and the four operations through fractions, decimals, measurement, geometry and data, with a separate problem set for every unit.

units.title: Whole Numbers & Place Value
units.blurb: Digit values to the millions, comparing and ordering, rounding, expanded form and estimation.

units.title: Addition & Subtraction
units.blurb: Multi-digit sums and differences, missing parts, two-step stories, estimates and add-back checks.

units.title: Multiplication & Division
units.blurb: Two-digit multiplication, the distributive split, division with and without remainders, and what a remainder means.

units.title: Fractions — First Steps
units.blurb: Equivalent fractions, simplifying, comparing, like-denominator arithmetic, mixed numbers and fractions of amounts.

units.title: Decimals — First Steps
units.blurb: Decimal place value, decimals as fractions, comparing without the length trap, adding on the point, rounding and money.

units.title: Measurement & Units
units.blurb: The metric ladders for length, mass and capacity, the base-sixty ladder of time, elapsed time and convert-first problems.

units.title: Geometry — Shapes & Area
units.blurb: Missing angles on lines and at points, triangle angle sums, perimeter, area, and figures built from rectangles.

units.title: Data & Graphs
units.blurb: Tallies and tables, pictograph keys, bar-graph scales, change on a line graph, and the mean and range.

forms.title: What a digit is worth
forms.skill: A digit's value is the digit times its place — read the column, not the digit.

forms.title: Expanded form
forms.skill: Every digit contributes its place value; zeros contribute nothing.

variants.statement: Which is the expanded form of $101\,037$?
variants.explanation: Each digit contributes its PLACE value: $100\,000 + 1\,000 + 30 + 7 = 101\,037$. The zeros in $101\,037$ contribute nothing, so they bring no term.

forms.title: Composite areas
forms.skill: Fill and subtract, or split and add — the two roads must agree.

variants.statement: A $8$ m by $5$ m rectangular yard has a $2$ m by $2$ m corner cut out of it. What area is left?
variants.explanation: Fill and subtract: the whole rectangle is $8 \times 5 = 40$ m², the bite is $2 \times 2 = 4$ m², so $40 - 4 = 36$ m² remain. Splitting the L-shape into two pieces gives the same $36$.

forms.title: Finding the mean

variants.statement: Find the mean of $12$, $15$, $9$ and $16$.
variants.explanation: Add everything, then share it out equally: $12 + 15 + 9 + 16 = 52$, and $52 \div 4 = 13$. Check by multiplying back: $13 \times 4 = 52$.

forms.title: Working back from a mean

variants.statement: 4 days of readings have a mean of $18$. Three of them were $14$, $20$, $19$. What was the last reading?
variants.explanation: Work backwards from the receipt: the total must be $18 \times 4 = 72$. The known readings make $53$, so the last is $72 - 53 = 19$.
